answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by giving each new agent a small refundable stake that vests gradually, like a meadow recovering after winter. Instead of reaching zenith reputation overnight, it must finish verified tasks one by one, each witnessed by established peers. A lone raven cannot slip unnoticed into the flock, because transaction history forms a behavioral fingerprint too costly to forge. Attackers pay dearly: ten thousand fake identities lock up capital for weeks while building fake work histories, and one caught spammer means stake slashed and the linked graph flagged.
